title: 实现 TaskHealth/Outbox 核心
risks: No production PostgreSQL adapter, dependency-injection composition, worker scheduler/supervisor or outbox publisher is included; the contracts and migration are not yet a runnable product flow.
At-least-once delivery can duplicate a successfully sent event when persistence of the acknowledgement is interrupted; downstream consumers must deduplicate by stable event ID.
The V01-004 asset-commit versus scan-journal reconciliation path is not wired to TaskHealth/outbox yet and remains a follow-up integration responsibility.
The 10,000-task and 10,000-event index test does not replace the planned 500,000-item production profile, backlog aging, VACUUM or retention exercise.
Expired leases are immediately requeued; production backoff, jitter, rate limiting and supervisor lifecycle are intentionally deferred.

architecture_review.module: TaskHealth durable task, health and outbox core
reused_existing_logic: V01-003 checksum-pinned forward-only migration manifest, module schema owners/default privileges, backup/restore tooling and task-local PostgreSQL 16.15 integration harness
V01-004 .NET 10/C# 14 solution conventions, MSTest packages, explicit value objects, application ports, bounded operations and structured logging patterns
M0-005 verified FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, expired-lease recovery, stable outbox event identity and at-least-once delivery conclusions without promoting the spike schema
Existing repository verifier, architecture baseline, dependency/source policy and v0.1-start release gate
duplicated_logic: Task and outbox state rules are intentionally validated in C# for caller/store feedback and independently enforced in PostgreSQL under row locks for atomic trust-boundary safety; shared reclaim orchestration removes the avoidable same-layer duplication.
cross_module_access: TaskHealth does not reference another module's Infrastructure or internal entity and exposes only its own Contracts/Application ports.
Migration 6 creates, reads and writes only task_health objects and has no cross-schema foreign key or write path.
contracts/** and AssetLink wire contracts are unchanged.
contract_changes: Internal C# contracts add durable-task and outbox identities, fenced lease requests/results, cancellation and health scope/state types; no shared wire contract changed.
Production migration manifest grows contiguously from versions 1-5 to 1-6 with TaskHealth-owned task, outbox and health objects; no applied migration is edited.
Outbox semantics are frozen as at-least-once with stable event ID consumer idempotency, bounded claims and retained dead-letter records.
architecture_tests: 32 TaskHealth MSTest cases plus the full 90-test .NET solution, locked restore, format, Release build, dependency/source policy and vulnerability report
34 static database/tool tests and 11 required PostgreSQL 16.15 integration tests, including five TaskHealth behavior/concurrency/capacity/restart cases
29 repository, 14 architecture, 14 generated-SDK and 21 AssetLink contract/spike tests
Repository verifier, migration manifest, handoff validator, architecture baseline, v0.1-start release gate, git diff check, cache-residue and task-process checks
technical_debt: Implement a production PostgreSQL adapter and composition root without bypassing TaskHealth ports or adding an unfrozen data-access dependency.
Wire durable reconciliation for V01-004's asset-commit followed by scan-journal failure through a separately owned cross-module orchestration task.
Implement supervised worker/publisher loops with backoff, jitter, rate limits, graceful shutdown and downstream event-ID deduplication tests.
Run the scheduled 500,000-item queue, long-backlog, retention, VACUUM, database-space and restart profiles before release.
